events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 9 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The GPS track shows the trip was driven 24.9 km against an optimal route of 21.8 km, i.e. 3.1 km (+14%) more than the shortest and most direct route, contradicting the driver's claim that the fare is unimpeachable. [F1 F10] [RD-1 RD-2]
C2: Two distinct off-route segments are recorded: 22:57–23:03 adding 1.14 km and 23:21–23:24 adding 1.51 km, each deviating up to ~1 km from the optimal route, so they are unexempted deviation segments under RD-1. [F3 F4] [RD-1]
C3: No traffic incident (Accident/Roadwork/Breakdown/Block/Heavy Traffic) was recorded near the optimal route in the trip window, so the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' explanation has no traffic-fact support under RD-4(a). [F13 F10] [RD-4]
C4: The only traffic records are speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard during 22:34–23:40 — moderate flow, not band 1 or 2 — so even as corroboration RD-4(b) cannot justify the detours, and it never exempts a segment on its own. [F11 F12] [RD-4]
C5: The chat contains only pickup logistics (rider at main entrance 22:40, driver arriving 22:40); there is no message in which the driver proposed a route change before leaving the optimal route or the rider agreed to one, so RD-5 does not exempt either segment. [F8 F9 F10] [RD-5 RD-3]
C6: The ride was completed at 23:35 with pickup at 22:45 (F2 shows 50.2 min actual vs 28 min estimate), so the delay is not explained by a rider-requested stop: the chat shows no stop request and there is no waiting charge in the bill ($0.00 waiting). [F2 F7 F8] [RD-3 RD-1]
C7: This is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so extra kilometres enter the fare: the billed distance component was $35.17 for 24.9 km at $1.41/km and the fare system itself priced the 3.1 km excess at $4.41. [F5 F7] [RD-2]
C8: Refund is limited to the metered distance units of the two unexempted segments: (1.14 km + 1.51 km) × $1.41/km = $3.74, rounded to the cent, the rest of the 3.1 km being map-matching residual; no waiting fee was charged so none is disputed. [F3 F4 F5 F7] [RD-2]
C9: The driver's 90-day record already shows 1 upheld dispute, so this now-upheld route deviation makes the case 'repeated' and warrants an account-review flag in addition to the refund. [F16 F3 F4] [RD-6]

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the trip was driven 24.9 km against an optimal route of 21.8 km, i.e. 3.1 km (+14%) more than the shortest and most direct route, contradicting the driver's claim that the fare is unimpeachable.

Two distinct off-route segments are recorded: 22:57–23:03 adding 1.14 km and 23:21–23:24 adding 1.51 km, each deviating up to ~1 km from the optimal route, so they are unexempted deviation segments under RD-1.

No traffic incident (Accident/Roadwork/Breakdown/Block/Heavy Traffic) was recorded near the optimal route in the trip window, so the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' explanation has no traffic-fact support under RD-4(a).

The only traffic records are speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard during 22:34–23:40 — moderate flow, not band 1 or 2 — so even as corroboration RD-4(b) cannot justify the detours, and it never exempts a segment on its own.

The chat contains only pickup logistics (rider at main entrance 22:40, driver arriving 22:40); there is no message in which the driver proposed a route change before leaving the optimal route or the rider agreed to one, so RD-5 does not exempt either segment.

The ride was completed at 23:35 with pickup at 22:45 (F2 shows 50.2 min actual vs 28 min estimate), so the delay is not explained by a rider-requested stop: the chat shows no stop request and there is no waiting charge in the bill ($0.00 waiting).
This is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so extra kilometres enter the fare: the billed distance component was $35.17 for 24.9 km at $1.41/km and the fare system itself priced the 3.1 km excess at $4.41.

Refund is limited to the metered distance units of the two unexempted segments: (1.14 km + 1.51 km) × $1.41/km = $3.74, rounded to the cent, the rest of the 3.1 km being map-matching residual; no waiting fee was charged so none is disputed.
The driver's 90-day record already shows 1 upheld dispute, so this now-upheld route deviation makes the case 'repeated' and warrants an account-review flag in addition to the refund.

weaknesses: The driver will point to F11/F12 (speed band 3 on ECP and Airport Boulevard during 22:34–23:40) and argue congestion justified avoiding those roads; we must concede band 3 is real but note it is neither band 1 nor 2 and has no incident record (F13), so it does not meet RD-4.

The driver's statement in F10 ('I followed my GPS') is a plausible-sounding explanation, and the rider produced no message in F8/F9 objecting during the trip, which the driver can spin as tacit acceptance; RD-5 still requires prior driver notice plus explicit consent, which is absent.

The GPS excess is 3.1 km (F1) but the two recorded off-route segments only add 2.65 km (F3+F4), so we can only claim $3.74, not the full $4.41 billed excess in F5 — the ~0.45 km gap is map-matching residual the policy does not refund (RD-2).

The driver's profile (F16) is long and busy (5.7 y, 1165 trips, only 1 upheld dispute), and the rider's own record (F15) shows 2 disputes with 0 upheld, which the other side can use to argue this is a pattern of unfounded rider complaints.

events.title: Driver Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
D1: The two off-route segments are 1.14 km (22:57–23:03) and 1.51 km (23:21–23:24), totalling 2.65 km of extra distance, while the ride was 3.1 km over the optimal 21.8 km; the remaining ~0.45 km is map-matching residue that is not refundable under RD-2. [F1 F3 F4] [RD-1 RD-2]
D2: This is a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter (24.9 km at $1.41/km distance plus 50.2 min time), so any refund is limited to the unforgiven extra mileage at the per-km rate and must exclude waiting and the non-mileage part of the fare. [F5 F7] [RD-2]
D3: No traffic incident was recorded anywhere near the optimal route during the trip window, and the only speed-band evidence (band 3, 20–29 km/h on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) is weaker than the band 1–2 congestion RD-4 requires, so neither segment qualifies for the reasonable-cause exemption under RD-4(a) and the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' statement cannot defeat the GPS record. [F10 F11 F12 F13] [RD-4]
D4: The chat contains no route-change request from the rider before either segment — the only messages are pick-up logistics at 22:40 — so the driver cannot claim prior passenger agreement to the detour under RD-5. [F3 F4 F8 F9] [RD-5]
D5: The refund on the two segments should be 2.65 km × $1.41/km = $3.74, rounded to the cent, i.e. 1.14 km × $1.41 = $1.61 plus 1.51 km × $1.41 = $2.13, which matches the billed excess-rate of $4.41 on 3.1 km for the mileage actually driven beyond the optimal route. [F3 F4 F5 F7] [RD-2]
D6: The driver pressed neither an arrival nor a waiting charge issue into this dispute and the waiting fee is $0.00 with no surge, so no additional item beyond the deviation mileage is in scope. [F6 F7] [FARE-1]
D7: Because a refund greater than zero is owed on the deviation, and the driver's 90-day history shows one upheld dispute but zero route disputes upheld, RD-6's flag_account trigger (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met, so the account flag should not be added on this record. [F15 F16] [RD-6]
Weaknesses: The GPS record itself establishes unforgiven deviation: F3 and F4 show 2.65 km of off-route driving up to 985 m from the optimal route, with no prior rider agreement in the chat (F8, F9), so a partial refund under RD-2 is unavoidable and the best available outcome is to cap it, not to escape it. | F1 and F2 show +3.1 km and +21.8 min against the estimate; the rider will argue the whole excess, and the fare facts (F5, F7) show the excess was billed at $4.41, so the driver cannot argue the meter was unaffected. | The driver's written statement (F10) offers only 'I followed my GPS', which is a statement contradicted by the system records (F3, F4, F13) and therefore carries no weight against them. | Traffic was mildly slow (band 3, 20–29 km/h on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard, F11, F12), which the rider may try to convert into an argument that a reroute was needed — but band 3 does not meet RD-4(a) or (b), and it equally shows the driver had no congestion excuse.
Asks: refund_partial $3.74

No traffic incident was recorded anywhere near the optimal route during the trip window, and the only speed-band evidence (band 3, 20–29 km/h on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) is weaker than the band 1–2 congestion RD-4 requires, so neither segment qualifies for the reasonable-cause exemption under RD-4(a) and the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' statement cannot defeat the GPS record.

The chat contains no route-change request from the rider before either segment — the only messages are pick-up logistics at 22:40 — so the driver cannot claim prior passenger agreement to the detour under RD-5.

The driver pressed neither an arrival nor a waiting charge issue into this dispute and the waiting fee is $0.00 with no surge, so no additional item beyond the deviation mileage is in scope.

Because a refund greater than zero is owed on the deviation, and the driver's 90-day history shows one upheld dispute but zero route disputes upheld, RD-6's flag_account trigger (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met, so the account flag should not be added on this record.

weaknesses: The GPS record itself establishes unforgiven deviation: F3 and F4 show 2.65 km of off-route driving up to 985 m from the optimal route, with no prior rider agreement in the chat (F8, F9), so a partial refund under RD-2 is unavoidable and the best available outcome is to cap it, not to escape it.

F1 and F2 show +3.1 km and +21.8 min against the estimate; the rider will argue the whole excess, and the fare facts (F5, F7) show the excess was billed at $4.41, so the driver cannot argue the meter was unaffected.
The driver's written statement (F10) offers only 'I followed my GPS', which is a statement contradicted by the system records (F3, F4, F13) and therefore carries no weight against them.

Traffic was mildly slow (band 3, 20–29 km/h on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard, F11, F12), which the rider may try to convert into an argument that a reroute was needed — but band 3 does not meet RD-4(a) or (b), and it equally shows the driver had no congestion excuse.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.74 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F7: distance component $35.17 over 24.9 km, time $13.04, platform $1.47), so under RD-2 the remedy runs on mileage units only: the per-km rate derived from the fare fact is $35.17 ÷ 24.9 km = $1.41/km [F7][RD-2]. The ride was driven 24.9 km against an optimal 21.8 km, a +3.1 km excess [F1], and two off-route segments are recorded: 22:57–23:03 adding 1.14 km and 23:21–23:24 adding 1.51 km, each up to ~985–970 m off the optimal route [F3][F4]. Under RD-1 each such segment must individually pass RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 scrutiny, and any unexplained deviation breaches the driver's shortest-and-most-direct-route duty [F3][F4][RD-1].

No exemption applies to either segment. There is no traffic incident near the optimal route during the trip window [F13], so there is no reasonable-cause evidence under RD-4(a); the only congestion records are speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard [F11][F12], which is above the band 1–2 threshold and, per RD-4(b), is corroborative only and cannot exempt a segment on its own [F11][F12][RD-4]. The driver's statement that his GPS rerouted him [F10] is a statement, and it is contradicted by the GPS record [F1][F3][F4], so it carries no weight under the procedural rule that system records override statements; it cannot manufacture a "reasonable cause" that no traffic fact supports [F10][F13][RD-4]. No prior driver route proposal or rider agreement appears anywhere in the chat — Chat #1 and Chat #2 at 22:40 are pickup logistics only [F8][F9] — so RD-5 exempts neither segment [F8][F9][F3][F4][RD-5]. There is likewise no rider-named stop or stop request, and the bill shows $0.00 waiting [F7][F8][RD-3]. Both segments are therefore unexempted deviation segments.

The refund is the sum of the unexempted segments' extra kilometres at the metered rate: 1.14 km × $1.41 = $1.61, plus 1.51 km × $1.41 = $2.13, i.e. $1.61 + $2.13 = $3.74 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The remaining ~0.45 km of the 3.1 km trip excess (the billed $4.41 excess versus $3.74 of segments) is map-matching residual and is not refundable under RD-2 [F1][F3][F4][F5][RD-2]. No waiting fee was charged and no surge applied, so nothing further is in scope under FARE-1 [F6][F7][FARE-1]. RD-6's flag condition is not met: the driver's 90-day profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 [F16], so a refund greater than zero is owed but no account-review flag attaches [F16][RD-6].

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the trip was driven 24.9 km against an optimal route of 21.8 km, i.e. 3.1 km (+14%) more than the shortest and most direct route, contradicting the driver's claim that the fare is unimpeachable.

Two distinct off-route segments are recorded: 22:57–23:03 adding 1.14 km and 23:21–23:24 adding 1.51 km, each deviating up to ~1 km from the optimal route, so they are unexempted deviation segments under RD-1.

No traffic incident (Accident/Roadwork/Breakdown/Block/Heavy Traffic) was recorded near the optimal route in the trip window, so the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' explanation has no traffic-fact support under RD-4(a).

The only traffic records are speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard during 22:34–23:40 — moderate flow, not band 1 or 2 — so even as corroboration RD-4(b) cannot justify the detours, and it never exempts a segment on its own.

The chat contains only pickup logistics (rider at main entrance 22:40, driver arriving 22:40); there is no message in which the driver proposed a route change before leaving the optimal route or the rider agreed to one, so RD-5 does not exempt either segment.

The ride was completed at 23:35 with pickup at 22:45 (F2 shows 50.2 min actual vs 28 min estimate), so the delay is not explained by a rider-requested stop: the chat shows no stop request and there is no waiting charge in the bill ($0.00 waiting).
This is a metered RydeTAXI ride, so extra kilometres enter the fare: the billed distance component was $35.17 for 24.9 km at $1.41/km and the fare system itself priced the 3.1 km excess at $4.41.

Refund is limited to the metered distance units of the two unexempted segments: (1.14 km + 1.51 km) × $1.41/km = $3.74, rounded to the cent, the rest of the 3.1 km being map-matching residual; no waiting fee was charged so none is disputed.
The driver's 90-day record already shows 1 upheld dispute, so this now-upheld route deviation makes the case 'repeated' and warrants an account-review flag in addition to the refund.

weaknesses: The driver will point to F11/F12 (speed band 3 on ECP and Airport Boulevard during 22:34–23:40) and argue congestion justified avoiding those roads; we must concede band 3 is real but note it is neither band 1 nor 2 and has no incident record (F13), so it does not meet RD-4.

The driver's statement in F10 ('I followed my GPS') is a plausible-sounding explanation, and the rider produced no message in F8/F9 objecting during the trip, which the driver can spin as tacit acceptance; RD-5 still requires prior driver notice plus explicit consent, which is absent.

The GPS excess is 3.1 km (F1) but the two recorded off-route segments only add 2.65 km (F3+F4), so we can only claim $3.74, not the full $4.41 billed excess in F5 — the ~0.45 km gap is map-matching residual the policy does not refund (RD-2).

The driver's profile (F16) is long and busy (5.7 y, 1165 trips, only 1 upheld dispute), and the rider's own record (F15) shows 2 disputes with 0 upheld, which the other side can use to argue this is a pattern of unfounded rider complaints.

claims.assertion: The two off-route segments are 1.14 km (22:57–23:03) and 1.51 km (23:21–23:24), totalling 2.65 km of extra distance, while the ride was 3.1 km over the optimal 21.8 km; the remaining ~0.45 km is map-matching residue that is not refundable under RD-2.

This is a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter (24.9 km at $1.41/km distance plus 50.2 min time), so any refund is limited to the unforgiven extra mileage at the per-km rate and must exclude waiting and the non-mileage part of the fare.

No traffic incident was recorded anywhere near the optimal route during the trip window, and the only speed-band evidence (band 3, 20–29 km/h on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard) is weaker than the band 1–2 congestion RD-4 requires, so neither segment qualifies for the reasonable-cause exemption under RD-4(a) and the driver's 'my GPS rerouted me' statement cannot defeat the GPS record.

The chat contains no route-change request from the rider before either segment — the only messages are pick-up logistics at 22:40 — so the driver cannot claim prior passenger agreement to the detour under RD-5.

The refund on the two segments should be 2.65 km × $1.41/km = $3.74, rounded to the cent, i.e. 1.14 km × $1.41 = $1.61 plus 1.51 km × $1.41 = $2.13, which matches the billed excess-rate of $4.41 on 3.1 km for the mileage actually driven beyond the optimal route.
The driver pressed neither an arrival nor a waiting charge issue into this dispute and the waiting fee is $0.00 with no surge, so no additional item beyond the deviation mileage is in scope.
